idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Why Your Toilet Keeps Running Non-Stop
description: A continuously running toilet is one of the most common causes of wasted water in Nigerian homes. In many cases, the problem starts inside the cistern rather than the bowl. When the fill valve fails or the float is set too high, the water level rises past the top of the vertical overflow tube. Water then flows constantly down into the toilet bowl to prevent your tank from overflowing onto the bathroom floor. Lowering the float adjustment screw can quickly fix the issue. If the water keeps rising after adjustment, the fill valve seal is likely worn and needs replacement by a professional plumber.
image_prompt: Crisp realistic vertical photograph looking down into the open inside of a white ceramic toilet cistern in a brightly lit modern bathroom. The ceramic tank lid is removed and resting beside the tank. Inside the water-filled cistern, a realistic modern plastic fill valve mechanism and a central vertical flush valve overflow tube are clearly visible. The water level inside the tank is slightly higher than the top rim of the vertical overflow tube, showing clear water gently spilling over the rim down into the pipe. High detail on water reflections, wet plastic components, smooth glazed porcelain, and natural indoor ambient lighting. Professional commercial photography, sharp focus, neutral visual space near the top and bottom. No text, no letters, no labels, no logos, no watermarks.
visual_story: The photograph offers an angled overhead look into an open, functioning toilet tank. The viewer immediately spots water spilling over the open top of the vertical overflow tube. This visual clearly explains how an incorrect water level or faulty valve creates a silent, continuous leak straight down into the bowl.

on_image_text.explanation: Water is overflowing directly into the vertical overflow tube inside the tank.
on_image_text.takeaway: Adjust your float level or replace a worn fill valve to save water.
